items.title: Finite-regulator outside density and entropy
items.statement:
Let $H_{\rm in}$ and $H_{\rm out}$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H_{\rm in}\otimes H_{\rm out}$. Choose orthonormal bases $(e_i)_{i=1}^{d_{\rm in}}$ and $(f_a)_{a=1}^{d_{\rm out}}$, and use the ordered product basis $(e_i\otimes f_a)$, with the $H_{\rm in}$ index first. The outside density $\rho_{\rm out}:H_{\rm out}\to H_{\rm out}$ is the linear map whose matrix entries in $(f_a)$ are

$$ (\rho_{\rm out})_{ab}:=\sum_{i=1}^{d_{\rm in}}\rho_{(i,a),(i,b)}. $$

Fix $k_B>0$ as a real scale. If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{d_{\rm out}}$ are the eigenvalues of $\rho_{\rm out}$ counted with multiplicity, define

$$ S_{\rm out}(\rho;H_{\rm in},H_{\rm out}):=-k_B\sum_{j=1}^{d_{\rm out}}\lambda_j\log\lambda_j, $$

where $\log$ is the natural logarithm and $0\log0:=0$. The finite matrix argument below proves that $\rho_{\rm out}$ is a density operator and that the displayed endomorphism is basis-independent, so $S_{\rm out}$ is a finite real number independent of the chosen bases. In this mathematical definition $k_B$ is only a positive scalar; no physical units or model are asserted.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, section 2.1.3
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, section 5.2.1
John Preskill, Quantum Shannon Theory, Chapter 2, section 2.3
John Preskill, Quantum Shannon Theory, Chapter 10, section 10.2

items.title: Finite mode cutoffs can have unbounded entropy
items.statement:
Fix a real number $k_B>0$. For each integer $N\ge1$, let $H_{\rm in}=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product and basis $1$, and let $H_{{\rm out},N}=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes N}$ with the standard product inner product and product basis. Identify the product basis of $\mathbb C\otimes H_{{\rm out},N}$ with that of $H_{{\rm out},N}$. For the density operator $\rho_N=I_{2^N}/2^N$, where $I_{2^N}$ is the identity matrix on this $2^N$-dimensional space, the outside entropy is

$$ S_{\rm out}(\rho_N;\mathbb C,H_{{\rm out},N})=k_BN\log2, $$

which tends to $+\infty$ as $N\to\infty$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, section 5.2.1
John Preskill, Quantum Shannon Theory, Chapter 10, section 10.2

items.title: Finite subtraction ambiguity
items.statement:
Let $x=(x_N)_{N\ge1}$ and $r=(r_N)_{N\ge1}$ be real sequences, and let $L\in\mathbb R$. Here $x_N-r_N\to L$ means that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is an integer $N_0$ such that $|x_N-r_N-L|<\varepsilon$ for all $N\ge N_0$. For every $a\in\mathbb R$, the equally valid subtraction $r'_N=r_N-a$ satisfies

$$ x_N-r'_N\longrightarrow L+a. $$

Thus existence of a finite subtracted limit alone does not select its additive finite part; no particular divergence expansion or physical renormalization scheme is assumed.

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.100B Real Analysis, Spring 2025 full lecture notes, Lecture 3, sequence convergence definition

items.title: Additive entropy definition does not imply monotonicity
items.statement:
Let $s\in\mathbb R$ be a fixed additive term, let $H_{\rm in}=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product and basis $(1)$, and let $H_{\rm out}=\mathbb C^2$ with its standard inner product and orthonormal basis $(f_0,f_1)$. In the ordered product basis $(1\otimes f_0,1\otimes f_1)$, set the joint density matrices $\rho_0=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&0\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\rho_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$. On the ordered two-point set $\{0,1\}$ define $G(t):=s+S_{\rm out}(\rho_t;H_{\rm in},H_{\rm out})$. Then

$$ G(1)=G(0)-k_B\log2<G(0). $$

This is a finite matrix comparison for an additive definition; the labels $0,1$ do not describe a physical evolution.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, section 5.2.1
John Preskill, Quantum Shannon Theory, Chapter 10, section 10.2
